findings.title: Counter scaling immediately overwritten
findings.description: Step 4 scales the counter for multiplier tier changes, but Step 5 immediately recalculates and overwrites it using the original counter value. This loses the scaling and causes unintended decay jumps when kepuasan transitions between multiplier tiers.
findings.evidence: Line 289-293: Scale counter at step 4, then line 293 overwrites with: newRatingMonthCounter = ratingMonthCounter + (monthsPassed * newMultiplier);
findings.consequence: Player experiences unintended decay jumps when kepuasan crosses tier boundaries. Smooth transitions not working as designed.
findings.correction: Line 293 should be: newRatingMonthCounter = newRatingMonthCounter + (monthsPassed * newMultiplier); (use updated counter, not original)

findings.title: Low sector penalty system not ported to fractional system
findings.description: The getDecayMultiplierFromSatisfaction() function does not accept lowSectorCount parameter and does not apply sector penalties. The old system capped threshold to 6 months when low sectors existed, but this logic is missing in the new multiplier system.
findings.evidence: Parameter lowSectorCount defined at line 264 but never used. Function getDecayMultiplierFromSatisfaction() at lines 46-79 has no lowSectorCount parameter and no sector penalty logic.
findings.consequence: Low sectors no longer affect rating decay. Game balance affected; player can ignore low sectors without decay penalty.
findings.correction: Add lowSectorCount parameter to getDecayMultiplierFromSatisfaction() and apply equivalent sector penalty to multiplier (e.g., reduce multiplier by 5% per low sector up to limit).

findings.title: Caller default threshold value incompatible with new multiplier semantics
findings.description: Both callers (map-system.tsx and npcCountrySimulation.ts) default lastRatingThreshold to 12, which is the old threshold system (months). The new system uses multipliers (0.1-1.0), so default should be 1.0 for healthy kepuasan.
findings.evidence: map-system.tsx line 5326: lastRatingThreshold: prev.last_rating_threshold ?? 12; npcCountrySimulation.ts line 373: lastRatingThreshold: Number(country.last_rating_threshold) || 12;
findings.consequence: New games and games without saved lastRatingThreshold will use 12 as the multiplier, which clamps to 1.0 then scales counter incorrectly via the broken Step 4 logic. Decay rate unpredictable.
findings.correction: Change defaults to 1.0 instead of 12: lastRatingThreshold: prev.last_rating_threshold ?? 1.0

findings.title: No migration strategy for existing saves with old threshold format
findings.description: Old saves store last_rating_threshold in range [1-12] (months-based thresholds). New code interprets this field as a multiplier in range [0.1-1.0]. When an old save loads, the semantic mismatch causes wrong decay calculations.
findings.evidence: Old system: 12 months threshold for healthy kepuasan. New system: 1.0 multiplier for healthy kepuasan. On load, old threshold=12 is interpreted as multiplier=12, clamped to 1.0, causing counter scaling issues at Step 4 (which is then overwritten anyway).
findings.consequence: Existing saves will have incorrect decay rates on first load. Rating decay may be too fast or too slow depending on the saved threshold value. Player experience inconsistent.
findings.correction: Add migration logic: detect if last_rating_threshold is in [1-12] range (old system), convert to equivalent multiplier (e.g., 12 months -> 1.0, 1 month -> 0.1), and store as the new multiplier value.
